create.name: Bodhipaksa
create.bio:
Bodhipaksa is a Scottish-born Buddhist teacher who has lived in New Hampshire for many years. He began meditating in 1982 and was ordained into the Triratna Buddhist Order in 1993, receiving a name that means 'wings of enlightenment'. Before settling in the United States he ran the Dhanakosa retreat centre in the Scottish Highlands and then the Edinburgh Buddhist Centre, and later spent three years teaching Buddhist meditation to students in Montana's university religion programme while finishing a master's degree.

Out of that university work grew Wildmind, an online meditation centre he started in 2000 and still runs from Newmarket. Its free pages give step-by-step instruction in mindfulness of breathing, lovingkindness, walking meditation and the six element reflection, along with notes on posture. A small monthly contribution from supporters keeps the site free of advertising and gives them daily sits on Zoom, a private community, regular mini-retreats and a library of more than forty courses. Among his books are Living as a River, which looks at impermanence and not-self; This Difficult Thing of Being Human, a guide to being kinder to oneself; and a book of daily readings, A Year of Buddha's Wisdom; and he has recorded several albums of guided meditation. He also teaches at meditation centres in person.

books.title: This Difficult Thing of Being Human: The Art of Self-Compassion
books.author: Bodhipaksa
books.description: A practical book on self-compassion drawn from Buddhist practice. Bodhipaksa explains why kindness towards ourselves matters and offers short exercises for meeting difficult moments with more care.

books.title: Living as a River: Finding Fearlessness in the Face of Change
books.author: Bodhipaksa
books.description: An exploration of the Buddhist teaching of not-self built around the traditional six element reflection. Readers are led through earth, water, fire, air, space and consciousness to see how little of what we take as 'me' is fixed.

books.title: Wildmind: A Step-by-Step Guide to Meditation
books.author: Bodhipaksa
books.description: An illustrated beginner's manual that grew out of the Wildmind website. It sets out posture and the two core Buddhist practices of mindfulness of breathing and lovingkindness in clear stages.

courses.title: Wildmind Community-Supported Meditation Initiative
courses.description: Supporters fund the ad-free Wildmind site and in return join daily meditation sittings on Zoom, a private online community and monthly mini-retreats. They also get rolling access to more than forty of Bodhipaksa's online courses, from a ten-day introduction to month-long series on kindness and compassion.
courses.price: $8 USD a month, plus a one-time $40 USD joining fee

free_resources.title: Bodhipaksa on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Bodhipaksa's free Insight Timer page, where his guided Buddhist meditations and talks can be played in the app or a web browser at no cost.

free_resources.title: Learn the Mindfulness of Breathing Meditation
free_resources.description: A free, staged written guide to the most widely taught Buddhist sitting practice, attending to the physical feel of the breath. Each of the four stages has its own page with tips on common difficulties.

free_resources.title: A complete guide to lovingkindness meditation
free_resources.description: Wildmind's free step-by-step introduction to metta bhavana, the practice of developing kindness, moving from oneself to a friend, a stranger, someone difficult and finally all beings.

free_resources.title: The six element practice
free_resources.description: A free written guide to a reflection from the Pali canon on earth, water, fire, air, space and consciousness, used to loosen the sense of a fixed self.

flags: Tier borderline: ~83.8k from Insight Timer alone (80k–150k band). He is a long-standing author with Sounds True and Parallax Press; the owner may judge editorial stature.

Wildmind has free sections on meditation and depression, pain and stress; those were not used (health rule). The site as a whole is general meditation teaching.
